skill.name: lark-openapi-explorer
skill.description: Explores official Feishu and Lark OpenAPI Markdown documentation when existing lark-cli commands or skills do not cover a request. It identifies native endpoint details and prepares guarded lark-cli api calls.
skill.summary: Find official Lark or Feishu OpenAPI endpoints and prepare safe lark-cli api calls.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-focused and contains no evidence of prompt injection, obfuscation, credential theft, or arbitrary filesystem traversal. The real security concern is intentional external lark-cli api execution, including examples for state-changing Lark or Feishu API calls. Existing safety language requires confirmation for write and delete actions, but marketplace users should treat this as a command-executing API automation skill.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution for native OpenAPI calls
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before every lark-cli api invocation that changes data, and show the method, path, tenant target, and payload summary first.

remediation.issue: Broad OpenAPI exploration can reach sensitive tenant operations
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege scope checks and refuse destructive endpoints unless the user confirms the exact affected resource.
Keep WebFetch usage limited to official Feishu and Lark documentation domains, and never place secrets or tokens in URLs or prompts.

content.value_statement: Lark and Feishu tasks sometimes need APIs that are not wrapped by existing CLI commands. This skill finds official endpoint docs and prepares safer lark-cli api calls.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether existing Lark skills or lark-cli commands already cover a request.
Uses official Feishu and Lark documentation indexes to locate relevant API modules.
Extracts endpoint methods, paths, parameters, permissions, response fields, and error codes.
Prepares lark-cli api call guidance for native OpenAPI endpoints.
Translates Chinese API documentation details for English-speaking users.
Applies confirmation guidance before write or delete operations.
limitations: Requires a working lark-cli installation and valid authentication outside the skill.
Depends on official documentation accuracy and availability.
Cannot guarantee the caller has required tenant permissions or API scopes.
State-changing calls still need careful human confirmation before execution.

use_cases.title: Handle Unwrapped Team Admin Tasks
use_cases.description: Find the official endpoint for a Lark admin action that is not available through existing CLI commands.

use_cases.title: Build Internal Automation Safely
use_cases.description: Identify endpoint requirements before adding a native Lark or Feishu API call to an internal workflow.

use_cases.title: Translate API Documentation Into Action
use_cases.description: Convert Chinese OpenAPI documentation into a concise English summary with permissions and request requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Missing API
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery for an unsupported task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the official Lark or Feishu OpenAPI endpoint for this task: [describe task]. First check whether an existing skill or lark-cli command already covers it.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Understand one API before using it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the official documentation for this endpoint and summarize its method, path, required parameters, permissions, response fields, and common errors.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Call
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a request that may change data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the safest lark-cli api call plan for [endpoint goal]. Show the target resource, side effects, required scopes, and confirmation question before any execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reusable Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow planning across related endpoints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the official Lark OpenAPI documentation for [workflow]. Propose a step-by-step automation plan with read checks, write confirmations, rollback notes, and permission requirements.

output_examples.input: Find how to add members to a Lark group when the normal CLI command is unavailable.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the chat member endpoint, lists required identifiers and permissions, explains the side effect, and asks for confirmation before any write action.

output_examples.input: Explain the API needed to update a group announcement in English.
output_examples.output: The response gives the endpoint purpose, required revision value, content field expectations, permission scope, and common failure cases in plain English.

output_examples.input: Check whether there is a native API for a workflow not covered by lark-cli.
output_examples.output: The response checks existing CLI coverage, searches official documentation modules, and returns candidate endpoints with confidence and next verification steps.

best_practices: Start by checking existing lark-cli commands before exploring native OpenAPI endpoints.
Use official Feishu or Lark documentation as the source for every path and parameter.
Confirm tenant, resource, permissions, and side effects before any write or delete call.
anti_patterns: Do not guess endpoint paths, parameters, or permission scopes without opening official documentation.
Do not run write or delete requests without explicit user confirmation.
Do not place secrets, access tokens, or private user data in documentation fetch URLs.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a Lark or Feishu task is not covered by existing skills or lark-cli commands.

faq.question: Does it execute API calls automatically?
faq.answer: It can prepare lark-cli api calls, but write and delete actions should require explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Which documentation sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses official Feishu and Lark OpenAPI documentation indexes and endpoint pages.

faq.question: Can it work with English requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to translate Chinese documentation details into English when needed.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: You need lark-cli installed, authenticated, and granted the API scopes required by the selected endpoint.

faq.question: Is it safe for destructive operations?
faq.answer: It includes confirmation guidance, but destructive operations still require careful human review before execution.
